description: ARES Mars Explorer builds an interactive Jezero Crater map that compares terrain-aware routes using real DEM terrain and Perseverance MEDA data. It clearly labels measured, derived, and assumed values and leaves missing data unavailable. We are seeking a second participant interested in Mars, mapping, data visualization, or web development.
summary: ARES Mars Explorer is an interactive planning map for human exploration in Jezero Crater. It compares a direct reference line with two A* routes: the shortest traversable path and a route that minimizes a slope-based terrain cost. The map uses a real 20 m Mars 2020 CTX digital elevation model to derive slope and hillshade, and displays Perseverance MEDA measurements from sol 309 for pressure, wind, and air temperature. A four-hour out-and-back mission check helps users compare distance, terrain, and available on-site time. Every displayed value is labeled as measured, derived, or assumed, and missing data remains unavailable. The project is intentionally transparent about limits: route cost is not a safety rating, weather applies only at the rover location, and time estimates use stated assumptions.
details: ARES runs as a static web application. A Python preprocessing pipeline reads the projected 20 m CTX DEM, validates its coordinate reference system and coverage, computes slope and hillshade, and runs A* over known traversable cells. One route minimizes distance; the other minimizes accumulated slope penalty. The interface compares three scenarios, route length, maximum slope, out-and-back time, and remaining on-site time. A separate builder verifies Perseverance MEDA PDS4 labels and checks MD5 values, record counts, columns, and fill values before producing pressure, wind, and temperature charts. The pipeline never interpolates NoData cells. It labels source measurements, derived layers, and operational assumptions separately. The project includes 83 automated tests and reproducibility checks. Technologies: Python, NumPy, rasterio, pyproj, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet, GeoJSON, PNG overlays, and GitHub Pages. The design prioritizes traceability and honest uncertainty over unsupported safety claims. Super Intelligence tools assisted with coding, debugging, documentation editing, and submission drafting; project data sources, calculations, and outputs were reviewed against source metadata and automated tests.
